title: Why Sometimes It's Wiser to be Dumber
author: Ad Aeternum
summary: This article uses the internet trend of 'retardmaxxing' — deliberately stepping back from overthinking, metrics, and social comparison — to illuminate a principle the Christian tradition has long understood. The trend correctly identifies that paralysis-by-analysis prevents men from taking bold, purposeful action. However, the author argues it lacks metaphysical grounding: where the trend offers only contrarianism, Christianity offers a theological foundation for action uncoupled from outcomes. The Christian acts in a way that pleases God and leaves results to Him — which historically produced the boldest risk-takers who built Western culture. The Fahrenheit 451 quote grounds the argument: information overload creates the feeling of motion without movement. The author distinguishes between materialist calculation-dependence and Christian trust-grounded boldness.
points: The 'retardmaxxing' trend — deliberately tuning out metrics and social comparison — correctly identifies that overthinking paralyzes modern men.
Paralysis-by-analysis is treated as cautious wisdom but is actually a form of fear-slavery that prevents purposeful action.
Christianity offers metaphysical grounding for action uncoupled from outcomes: trust in God's will enables bold risk-taking that materialism cannot justify.
Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451 captures the problem: men stuffed with information feel they're thinking but are getting a sense of motion without moving.
The Christian acts to please God and leaves results to Him — historically producing the boldest and most world-building risk-takers.
quotes: Stop thinking so much, do what needs to be done, take risks, live a little.

Cram them full of non-combustible data, chock them so damned full of facts they feel stuffed, but absolutely brilliant with information. Then they'll feel they're thinking, they'll get a sense of motion without moving." — Ray Bradbury, Fahrenheit 451
The overthinker and the excessive analyzer believe on a certain level that it's their efforts and strategy which will determine the outcome of a certain project or action.
The Christian understands there are things beyond our understanding, and is thus much more willing to take the bold risks that lead to greatness.
Whereas the materialist bases his life and his choices exclusively on calculations, the Christian understands there are things beyond our understanding.
